commits.title: A payment stand-in for the end-to-end build: Stripe's API host can be pointed at a test server, never on Vercel

changes.how: A pure module modelled on viesEndpoint() in src/lib/vies.ts (read how src/server/vies.ts calls it: viesEndpoint({ testUrl: process.env.VIES_TEST_URL, allowTest: process.env.VIES_ALLOW_TEST_URL, vercel: process.env.VERCEL })). Export stripeEndpoint({ testUrl, allowTest, vercel }): returns null (Stripe's own API) unless ALL of these hold: vercel is empty or undefined, allowTest === '1', and testUrl parses as a URL whose protocol is 'http:' and whose hostname is '127.0.0.1' or 'localhost'; then it returns { host, port: Number(port), protocol: 'http' as const }. A doc comment says: a test server is honoured only with STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_URL=1, only on this machine's own address and never on Vercel, exactly as the VIES stand-in; the app has no other switch for it.

Unit test: null with nothing set; null with testUrl set and allowTest missing; null with both set and vercel '1'; null for 'https://127.0.0.1:3913' and for 'http://example.com:3913'; { host: '127.0.0.1', port: 3913, protocol: 'http' } for 'http://127.0.0.1:3913' with allowTest '1' and no vercel.

Import stripeEndpoint from '@/lib/stripe-endpoint'. Where OPTIONS is defined (apiVersion, maxNetworkRetries, timeout, appInfo) add the endpoint when there is one: const endpoint = stripeEndpoint({ testUrl: process.env.STRIPE_TEST_URL, allowTest: process.env.STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_URL, vercel: process.env.VERCEL }); const OPTIONS: Stripe.StripeConfig = { apiVersion: STRIPE_API_VERSION, maxNetworkRetries: 2, timeout: 15_000, appInfo: { name: 'Kaizena Flow' }, ...(endpoint ?? {}) }. The Stripe SDK's config takes host, port and protocol. Change nothing else in the file: stripeFor(), platformStripe() and the keys are read as before. Add the two variable names to .env.example with a comment 'end-to-end tests only; never set on Vercel' if src/lib/env-example.scan.test.ts requires every process.env name to be listed (run that test).

A node:http server in the style of e2e/fixtures/auth-stub.mjs (port from STRIPE_STUB_PORT, default 3913; GET /__health answers 200; every other path it does not know answers 404 with a Stripe-shaped error body and logs the method and path to standard error, so a missing endpoint is seen at once). It stands in for the calls the checkout's payment step makes. On 12 November the server-side calls on that path are: POST /v1/checkout/sessions (src/server/payment-session.ts line 261, ui_mode 'elements'; the code reads id and client_secret), POST /v1/coupons (line 249, only when the order has a discount code; the code reads id), GET /v1/checkout/sessions/{id} (src/server/checkout.ts line 1793, only after a payment returns, so not reached by this step) and GET /v1/payment_method_domains (src/server/express-checkout.ts line 200; ensurePaymentDomain() runs only for an https origin, so not reached on http://127.0.0.1). Answer the first two; confirm the list with rg -n 'stripe\.[a-zA-Z.]+\.(create|retrieve|update|list)\(' src/server/payment-session.ts src/server/checkout.ts src/server/payment-methods.ts src/server/express-checkout.ts, and look at how the integration tests fake the same calls (src/server/payment-methods.int.test.ts lines 15 to 30 return { id, url: null, client_secret: `${id}_secret` } for ui_mode 'elements'). Answer each with the smallest JSON the code reads, ids prefixed 'cs_test_e2e_' and a client secret of the same shape. Header comment: what it is, that it is the only fake of the payment path and is told it is one, and that the app reaches it only through STRIPE_TEST_URL with STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_URL=1.

Add the stand-in to webServer as the VIES stub is added (command 'node e2e/fixtures/stripe-stub.mjs', url http://127.0.0.1:<port>/__health, reuseExistingServer when not in CI, env STRIPE_STUB_PORT). In the env of the app's own entry ('pnpm start --port ...') add STRIPE_TEST_URL: `http://127.0.0.1:${stripePort}` and STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_URL: '1'. Do NOT add platform Stripe keys to that env for every spec: other specs rely on the server having none (e2e/draft-pay.spec.ts says so). The fixture store of the next commit gets its payments from its own rows.

commits.title: A fixture store that takes payments, a cart with two lines and the checkout at its payment step, measured and held

changes.how: Add a describe 'the money path'. Fixture, in beforeAll, made with SQL as e2e/draft-pay.spec.ts lines 54 to 62 do: const store = await testStore('betaling'); then insert into commerce.payment_providers (store_id, provider, enabled, active_mode) values (store.id, 'stripe', true, 'live') on conflict (store_id, provider) do update set enabled = true, active_mode = 'live'; and insert into commerce.stripe_accounts (store_id, mode, account_id, card_payments, requirements_due) values (store.id, 'live', 'acct_E2E<run>', 'active', false) on conflict (store_id, mode) do update set card_payments = 'active', requirements_due = false. A store made by testStore() is a copy of the template with its demo products. How the server gets a key for that store is already known and blocks this commit: paymentConnection() in src/server/payment-session.ts (line 108) builds the client only with platformStripe(found.mode), which reads STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_TEST / STRIPE_SECRET_KEY_LIVE from the server's environment; stripeFor() (a store's own key) is not on the checkout path, so there is no per-store key to give the fixture store. The end-to-end server has no platform keys on purpose (e2e/draft-pay.spec.ts asserts the problem its pay button shows without them). So before writing anything of this commit, stop and report to the owner the two ways forward, for the owner or a stronger model to choose: (a) platform test keys plus STRIPE_TEST_URL for the whole e2e server, and the specs whose expectations then change (at least e2e/draft-pay.spec.ts; list every spec that expects payments to be unavailable with rg -n -i 'not set up|cannot be followed|no stripe' e2e); (b) a second `pnpm start` of the same build on another port with the keys and the stand-in, used only by this describe. Do not pick one yourself. What follows is the rest of the commit once that choice is made. The cart: open a new phone context (390 by 844), go to two different products of the store and press Add to cart on each (use the selectors e2e/cart.spec.ts uses), then open the cart: expect two lines. The checkout: from the cart press the checkout button and fill the contact and delivery steps the way e2e/cart.spec.ts or e2e/pickup.spec.ts fills them, until the payment step shows. The browser's side of the provider: route the provider's script address with context.route('https://js.stripe.com/**', ...) to a small local file e2e/fixtures/stripe-js-stub.js that defines window.Stripe with the methods the checkout form calls (read src/components/checkout-form.tsx: the provider from @stripe/react-stripe-js with a clientSecret) and draws a box with data-testid 'payment-form-stub'; count the routed request as the one third-party request and its real size is not known to this test (say so in the table's comment: the nightly production run of step 1.14 reads the real script's bytes). Abort every other request to a host that is not the app's and collect its address: the list must be empty. Measures, each printed with E2E_MEASURE=1 as `[money] <page> <measure> <value>` and held at the figure times 1.05: for the two-line cart and for the checkout at its payment step: first scripts (the helper of step 1.3 on the HTML of the page's address, fetched with the context's cookies so the cart is the same) and the document (documentOf); router requests after load (the quiet rule; for the checkout: 0 router requests from the moment the payment form shows until three quiet seconds have passed); third-party requests: exactly one, the provider's script. Put the two pages' wire figures in WIRE_BUDGETS only if they are stable over two runs.

A plain browser script served by the test's route for https://js.stripe.com/**. It defines window.Stripe = function (key, options) returning an object with the methods the checkout's form calls; find the exact list by reading src/components/checkout-form.tsx and the @stripe/react-stripe-js provider it uses (initCheckout or elements, confirm, on, mount). Each method does the least that lets the form reach its shown state and never calls the network. A header comment: test-only, never bundled (it lives under e2e/), served only by e2e/performance.spec.ts's route.

The script already reads a JSON argument (`const args = JSON.parse(process.argv[3] ?? "{}")`, line 22) and measure() already passes a storageState for `spec.state` (line 92). Add three optional keys to that argument: moneyState (the path of a storage-state file), moneyCart and moneyCheckout (the two pages' paths, for example /s/<fixture slug>/no/cart). After the PAGES array, when all three are set, push two entries: `{ name: "store-cart-two-lines", group: "storefront", path: args.moneyCart, stateFile: args.moneyState, ...PHONE }` and `{ name: "store-checkout-payment", group: "storefront", path: args.moneyCheckout, stateFile: args.moneyState, ...PHONE }`; when any is missing print 'money path skipped: pass moneyState, moneyCart and moneyCheckout' once. In measure() change the storageState line to `storageState: spec.stateFile ?? (spec.state ? join(REPO, `e2e/.auth/${spec.state}.json`) : undefined),`. In the spec, when E2E_MEASURE=1, save the cart's browser state with `await context.storageState({ path: "e2e/.auth/money.json" })` once the cart has two lines and print `[money] address cart <path>` and `[money] address checkout <path>`. Document the three keys and how the state is made in the script's header and in docs/audits/bloat-review-2026-11/README.md.

Steps 0.43 and 1.1 make this file and step 1.3 adds its section '## The visitor's pages' (the two spec files, the E2E_MEASURE=1 switch, the two ratchet counts). Keep every line they wrote. Under '## The visitor's pages', after step 1.3's text, add a paragraph 'The money path': the fixture store, the payment stand-in (server side: STRIPE_TEST_URL with STRIPE_ALLOW_TEST_URL=1, never on Vercel; browser side: the test's own route), what is held for the two pages, and the sentence 'After phase 2 the two-line cart is judged against the bare store's bars, and the checkout at its payment step has first scripts of at most 670,000 bytes.' Lines of at most 130 characters.

Add a short section 'The end-to-end stand-in': the two variables, the three conditions under which the server uses a test address (the switch set, an address on this machine, not on Vercel), that production never sets them, and that no card data exists in the tests.
